subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Fitness Literacy II: Designing a Personal Program
title: Performance task build: sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days under transfer
focus: sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days
essentialQuestion: Can I write a program that I would actually finish?
privacySafeScenario: Write, run, and review a six-week personal program built around a self-chosen capability goal, documenting one mid-cycle revision and its reason.
studentTask: Learner works sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days applied to the learner’s own program while it is running, revised from what actually happened rather than from what was planned at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days applied to the learner’s own program while it is running, revised from what actually happened rather than from what was planned, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, balance, coordination, skill, or a functional task; any medical restriction is designed around with guardian input.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, balance, coordination, skill, or a functional task; any medical restriction is designed around with guardian input.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
